discovery: Discovery of organic superconductors and the establishment of molecular conductors as model systems for strongly correlated electrons

nominees.name: Denis Jérome
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Solides, Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Orsay, France

nominees.name: Gunzi Saito
nominees.affiliation: Toyota Physical and Chemical Research Institute / Kyoto University, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and superconductivity
motivation: In 1980 Jérome and Bechgaard discovered superconductivity under pressure in the Bechgaard salt (TMTSF)2PF6, the first superconductor built from organic molecules. Bechgaard designed the crystals and Jérome's high-pressure experiments showed how superconductivity emerges next to spin-density-wave order. Saito went on to develop the BEDT-TTF κ-phase salts. These include ambient-pressure superconductors near 12 K that border a Mott insulator, and κ-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu2(CN)3, the first experimental quantum spin liquid candidate. Together their work produced a whole family of clean, soft, chemically tunable crystals. In these crystals, pressure, strain and disorder move the system continuously across bandwidth-controlled Mott transitions, unconventional superconductivity, quasi-one-dimensional physics, Dirac electrons and spin liquids. These materials have become essential testing grounds for general ideas about electron correlation, close to the questions raised by cuprates. They are also a model of physicists and chemists working closely together.
